title: Coastal Clinic - POC scoping: quality eval plan
summary: POC scoping focused on quality evaluation plan. Agreed success criteria (accuracy and hallucination rates), workload sizing for pilot, benchmark metrics (latency, p95/p99), timeline for 2-week sandbox pilot then 6-week evaluation, and next steps to share golden prompt set and eval harness. Security concerns (SOC2, KMS, data residency) flagged and Redwood to share docs.
topics: Quality eval plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks
next_steps: Alex (AE) to send POC one-pager, pricing, and sandbox access (by 2026-11-19)
Priya (SE) to share quality eval template, golden prompts, and evaluation harness (by 2026-11-20)
Customer to provide representative dataset and 50 golden prompts (by 2026-11-23)
Schedule baseline benchmark run next week (target 2026-11-24)
Security: Redwood to share SOC2 report and KMS integration docs (by 2026-11-19)
action_items: Alex (AE) - Send POC agreement and trial credentials - due 2026-11-19
Priya (SE) - Upload eval harness + scripts to shared repo and walkthrough - due 2026-11-20
Sara (Customer) - Provide 50 golden prompts and 200 sample patient dialogues (de-identified) - due 2026-11-23
Mark (Customer Security) - Share minimum compliance checklist and data residency constraints - due 2026-11-20
transcript:
Header: 2026-11-18 15:00 UTC | Duration approx 52 minutes | Recording auto-generated by Fireflies
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Dr. Sara Nguyen (Coastal Clinic Head of AI), Tom Reyes (CTO), Lena Ortiz (PM), Mark Cho (Security)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick agenda, scoping the POC, define success criteria and quality eval plan, agree on workload and timeline.uh we'll start with introductions.
[00:12] Sara: Hi all, Sara here, we want to pilot a clinical note summarization assistant, primary goals are accuracy, no hallucination, and format adherence to our SOAP note template.
[00:25] Tom: CTO here, mainly concerned with throughput and latency, we have spikes during morning rounds, typically 60 concurrent users, average 3 requests per user per hour.
[00:36] Priya: Thanks Tom, when you say requests, are these full visit transcripts or short notes?
[00:40] Tom: Mostly full visit transcripts, average 800-1,200 tokens per request, with some longer ones to 2,000 tokens.
[00:47] Priya: got it. That helps for batching and KV cache sizing. (note: automatic transcript sometimes shows "K V cash")
[00:55] Lena: For success criteria, product wants 95% format compliance and <2% hallucination rate on critical fields (diagnoses/meds). We also want average latency under 1.2s per token or a p95 under 1.5s, whatever is realistic.
[01:12] Alex: Good, so preliminary success criteria captured: format compliance >=95%, hallucination <2% on critical fields, and latency p95 <1.5s. We'll refine scoring approach.
[01:21] Sara: Also, accuracy on entity extraction (medications/dosages) should be >90 F1 on our golden set.
[01:27] Priya: Perfect - that gives us an objective metric. We'll add regression tests to ensure F1 doesn't drop between model versions.
[01:35] Tom: Security - we need SOC2, data encryption at rest and in transit, and KMS for key management. We might require VPC/private deployment if we proceed beyond pilot.
[01:45] Mark: yes, also data residency: patient data must stay in us-east-1 for now, and audit logs are required.
[01:51] Alex: Redwood can provide SOC2 and KMS integration documentation; for the POC we can provision a private sandbox in a dedicated VPC if needed. I'll follow up with the security packet.
[02:02] Priya: Back to the quality eval plan - here's how we propose to structure it: 1) Golden prompt set - curated 50 prompts representing high-risk cases, 2) Regression suite - 500 examples with expected outputs for scoring, 3) Hallucination checks - a targeted test for hallucinated medications/diagnoses, 4) Format checks - automated parser that verifies SOAP fields and template adherence, 5) Scoring approach - composite score combining F1 on entities (50%), hallucination penalty (30%), and format compliance (20%).
[02:28] Sara: Can you explain the hallucination penalty more?
[02:31] Priya: Sure. For hallucination checks we use reference-grounded scoring: any assertion of a medical entity not present in the source transcript is a hallucination. We compute hallucination_rate = hallucinated_critical_fields / total_critical_fields_expected. Penalty reduces composite score proportionally; e.g., >2% hallucination triggers auto fail for pilot.
[02:47] Lena: That seems strict but ok for clinical safety. How do you handle partial matches? If model outputs 'metformin' vs 'metformine' spelled wrong?
[02:56] Priya: We use fuzzy match and normalize meds via RxNorm where possible; spelling variants that map to RxNorm count as match. We'll include normalization in the scoring script.
[03:08] Tom: Workload sizing: based on your numbers 60 concurrent users, ~3 req/hr, average 1,000 tokens => rough QPS isn't huge but concurrency matters for latency. For pilot let's simulate bursts up to 200 QPS for stress tests.
[03:21] Priya: Agreed. For the benchmark runs we'll provide two profiles: steady-state (10 qps) and burst (200 qps) with token distribution matching your logs (50% 800-1,200 tokens, 40% 200-800, 10% >1,500). We'll run p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec throughput.
[03:38] Sara: What models will you run? We prefer open models but we also care about cost.
[03:43] Alex: For the POC we suggest Redwood-verified model variants: 1) base open model quantized for cost, 2) high-accuracy variant (higher-cost), 3) fallback hosted variant for availability. We'll show cost vs latency tradeoffs in benchmark sheet.
[03:57] Priya: On evaluation harness: we'll push a small repo with scripts to call the API, compute metrics, and generate a report. It will include: golden prompts run (detailed manual review), regression suite scoring, hallucination detector output, and a per-field breakdown.
[04:14] Mark: Audit logs - we need request/response logging for X weeks and the ability to pull per-request IDs for debug. Is that available in the sandbox?
[04:22] Alex: Yes, sandbox will include request-level logs (redacted for PII if requested) and a sample trace for demonstration. We'll show how to enable audit retention.
[04:31] Lena: Timeline - we'd like to start pilot next week. Proposed: Week 0 (this week): share eval template and golden prompts; Week 1: sandbox integration + baseline benchmarks; Week 2: run regression and manual review, decision point end of Week 2. If good, expand to 6-week evaluation with more models.
[04:51] Priya: Timeline noted. For manual review we'll ask Coastal Clinic SMEs to review top 100 golden prompt outputs and flag failures. That manual review will be combined with automated metrics.
[05:03] Sara: What about hallucination detection automation? Can you detect factual contradictions to source?
[05:07] Priya: We'll do two layers: 1) automated heuristics (entity presence checks, negation detection) and 2) sample-based human review. Heuristics catch obvious hallucinations; humans catch nuanced hallucinations.
[05:20] Tom: Integration questions: do you support streaming outputs and function/tool calling? We use structured output to populate EHR fields.
[05:27] Alex: We support structured output and function calling; we'll include examples of JSON schema mapping to your SOAP template. Streaming is available for UX but for scoring we capture full response snapshots.
[05:39] Lena: Scoring thresholds recap: composite >= 0.8 (80%) for pass, hallucination_rate <2% mandatory, entity F1 >= 0.9 target. Is that correct?
[05:48] Priya: Yes, composite score with weights I mentioned earlier; we'll provide a spreadsheet that computes it per-run and across runs.
[05:56] Sara: Any red flags from Redwood?
[05:58] Alex: No red flags, just clarifications on data residency and how long logs persist. We'll follow up.
[06:04] Mark: If pilot moves to production we will require private deployment and annual SOC2 attestation.
[06:09] Alex: Understood; we'll outline deployment options and costs in the POC one-pager.
[06:15] Lena: Ok next steps then?
[06:17] Alex: I'll send POC paperwork + sandbox creds. Priya will share eval harness and golden prompt seed. Coastal to provide prompts + samples. We'll schedule baseline benchmark for Tuesday next week. Any other items?
[06:29] Sara: No, thanks. Looking forward to the eval.
[06:32] Alex: Great, thanks everyone.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-OT transcription (e.g., 'K V cash' instead of KV cache), filler words, and some speaker labels may be generic.
notes: Eval plan includes golden prompts (50), regression suite (500), hallucination checks, format parser for SOAP, composite scoring (F1 50%, hallucination penalty 30%, format 20%), pass threshold composite >=0.8 with hallucination <2% auto-fail.
